questions.question: Advantages of practicing mindfulness
questions.solution_html:
• Advantages of practicing mindfulness /[CO2]
  • Mindfulness is the practice of becoming more fully aware of the present moment- non
  • judgmentally and completely- rather than dwelling in the past or projecting into the future. It
  • generally involves a heightened awareness of sensory stimuli and ‘being in the now’.
  • Mindfulness is generally used to indicate both: 1. A state or quality of mind. 2. A form of
  • meditation that helps one to bring up and nurture this particular state or quality
  • Mindfulness helps reduce stress, increase self-awareness, and enhance emotional
  • regulation.And it lowers levels of distress and leads to a greater sense of well-being. In
  • general, mindfulness is associated with self-knowledge and well-being

questions.question: Discuss the significance of the sleep cycle and how it changes throughout the night.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the significance of the sleep cycle and how it changes throughout the night
  • [An / CO4]
  • The stages of the sleep cycle are vital for physical restoration, cognitive functioning, and
  • emotional well -being. A complete sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes, encompassing
  • NREM and REM sleep. Individuals progress through multiple cycles, starting with l onger
  • periods of deep NREM sleep (N2 and N3), crucial for physical recovery and immune
  • function. As the night continues, REM sleep durations increase, aiding memory
  • consolidation and emotional processing. This cyclical pattern allows the body to balance
  • restorative processes and cognitive functions, which is essential for overall health.

questions.question: Explain effective time management techniques and describe how can they improve goals setting processes.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain effective time management techniques and describe how can they
  • improve goals setting processes [A / CO5]
  • Eisenhower Matrix -Also known as Urgent - Important Matrix- The method helps
  • to prioritize tasks by urgency and importance while sorting out less urgent and important
  • tasks that you should either delegate or not do at all
  • Time management techniques is focused on time intervals - Pomodoro technique
  • Time Blocking -Scheduling specific blocks of time for different tasks or activities. It’s a
  • simple time management technique that helps you become aware and strategic of how you
  • spend your time. In time blocking, you divide your day into chunks of time—time blocks.
  • The Pareto principle, also known as the 80/20 rule, states that 80% of outcomes come from
  • 20% of causes
  • The ABCDE method is a time management technique where tasks are categorized based on
  • their urgency and importance, with "A" representing the most urgent and important tasks that
  • should be done first, and "E" representing the least important tasks that can be eliminated or
  • delegated; A (most important), B (important), C (nice to do, task with no
  • consequences), D (delegate), or E (eliminate whenever possible).
  • Some students may include (planning, scheduling tasks etc)

questions.question: Discuss about the various theories of dreaming.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss about the various theories of dreaming. / [CO4]
  • Psychoanalytic ,activation synthesis
  • One of the ways Freud devised to get at these early memories was to ex amine the dreams of
  • his patients, believing that conflicts, events, and desires of the past would be represented in
  • symbolic form in the dreams.Manifest & Latent content in dream- The manifest content of
  • a dream is the actual content of the dream itself
  • According to the activation-synthesis theory of dreaming, the pons in the brainstem sends
  • random signals to the upper part of the brain during REM sleep.
  • Hobson and colleagues have reworked the activation-synthesis hypothesis to reflect concerns
  • about dream meaning, calling it the Activation-information-mode model, or AIM (Hobson
  • et al., 2000). In this newer version, information that is accessed during waking hours can
  • have an influence on the synthesis of dreams
  • Some may also describe information processing and problem solving theory

questions.question: What is self confidence? Critically examine the theories and strategies of self confidence?
questions.solution_html:
• What is self confidence? Critically examine the theories and strategies of self confidence?
  • / [CO3]
  • Self-Confidence- belief in one's own abilities, qualities, and judgment, enabling individuals
  • to take risks and face challenges with a positive mindset.
  • Theories and strategies of self confidence- Adlerian, self concept, self efficacy, growth
  • mindset theory
  • Adlerian Theory of Self-ConfidencePsychologist Alfred Adler's theory suggests that early
  • experiences shape how people view themselves and the world. Children who are bullied or
  • marginalized may have difficulty with self-confidence and self-esteem as adults.
  • Self-concept TheoryCarl Rogers' theory suggests that self-confidence is closely linked to
  • self-concept, which is the perception and beliefs people have about themselves. Self-concept
  • is shaped by experiences, feedback, and social interactions.
  • Psychologist Albert Bandura's theory suggests that self-confidence is a cognitive
  • mechanism that influences people's motivation, thought patterns, emotional reactions, and
  • behavior. Self-efficacy is the belief that one can succeed in specific situations or accomplish
  • a task.
  • Growth mindset theory of self confidence- individuals who believe their abilities and
  • intelligence can be developed through effort and learning are more likely to cultivate self-
  • confidence and resilience in the face of challenges.
  • Psychologist Carol Dweck's theory suggests that people can improve their abilities and skills
  • through effort, feedback, and learning. People with a growth mindset see challenges as
  • opportunities to grow

questions.question: How do different types of social support influence emotional regulation, and what
questions.solution_html:
• psychological mechanisms contribute to its effectiveness? Illustrate your answer with
  • examples. [1] Social support is vital for managing difficult emotions by providing
  • emotional validation, practical assistance, and fostering resilience through various types—
  • emotional, informational, instrumental, and companionship support. It helps reduce stress,
  • anxiety, and depression by creating safe spaces for expression, offering guidance, and sharing
  • enjoyable activities. Psychological mechanisms, such as reducing stress hormones, promoting
  • emotional validation, enhancing resilience, and facilitating social learning, underpin its
  • effectiveness. For example, supportive relationships during life challenges, like a divorce, can
  • alleviate emotional burdens and provide practical help. However, the quality of support and
  • the recipient’s ability to utilize it constructively are crucial for its effectiveness.

questions.question: If you were to design a social competence training program for college students, what essential components would you include? Justify your choices with psychological theories and research. [2x15 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• If you were to design a social competence training program for college students, what
  • essential components would you include? Justify your choices with psychological theories
  • and research.. / [CO2]
  • An intervention program to enhance social competence should focus on:
  • Training in Communication Skills – Conducting workshops on active listening, assertive
  • communication, and non-verbal cues.
  • Role-Playing and Group Activities – Encouraging participation in simulated social
  • scenarios to practice handling real-life interactions.
  • Emotional Regulation Techniques – Teaching mindfulness, stress management, and
  • coping mechanisms for handling anxiety in social settings.
  • Conflict Resolution Strategies – Helping students develop problem-solving techniques to
  • address misunderstandings and disagreements constructively.
  • Building Peer Support Networks – Creating mentorship or buddy programs to foster a
  • sense of belonging and inclusivity.
  • By incorporating these strategies, students can develop stronger interpersonal skills,
  • improve confidence in social settings, and enhance their overall well-being.
